title: IIU investigating after Manitoba First Nation Police officer stabbed - Brandon Sun
subtitle: Breaking News, Sports, Manitoba, Canada
article: The Independent Investigations Unit of Manitoba is investigating after a man was shot and a police officer stabbed on Waywayseecappo First Nation on Wednesday.

Manitoba First Nations Police responded to a disturbance at the Waywayseecappo Gaming Centre Wednesday around 10:45 p.m. As one male was being arrested, a 21-year-old male began repeatedly stabbing the officer, according to a press release from the IIU.

The 29-year-old officer shot the second male and both were transported to hospital. According to the RCMP, the suspect is in serious but stable condition. The police officer was treated for serious injuries and has since been released from hospital.
Several individuals contacted The Brandon Sun overnight, stating that a Manitoba First Nations Police officer had been stabbed outside the First Nation gaming centre.
"First Nation Police officer stabbed," wrote in one individual who wished to remain anonymous, "and one male shot at Waywayseecappo First Nation VLT centre."

Waywayseecappo Chief Murray Clearsky confirmed this morning that an incident involving a Manitoba First Nations Police officer and at least one other individual had taken place late last night in the parking lot of the gaming centre.

Although one of the unconfirmed accounts sent to the Sun suggested one of the suspects in the incident was dead, Chief Clearsky stated that as of 3 a.m. last night, the two individuals who had been injured in the altercation - the officer and one of the suspects - were both in stable condition in hospital. He said he was unaware of any deaths as a result of the incident.
Chief Clearsky stated that all individuals in the altercation had been found and detained, and that RCMP were investigating. He declined to go into greater detail this morning.
The Sun has reached out and is waiting for confirmation of RCMP involvement.
